findings.title: Auto-generation design does not bind the attachment to the claimed course before save, file retrieval, or generation

sourceEvidence.explanation: The operation accepts independent attachmentId and courseId inputs, while its assigned matrix row declares no resourceInputs and the FLASH policy does not state the required Attachment→SyllabusItem→Course equality.

The existing save contract can create a course-linked deck from caller-supplied cards before resolving enrollment, attachment, or the attachment's persisted course. This baseline illustrates the authorization branch the revised design must explicitly close.
Enrollment is checked for the claimed course, but the attachment is fetched independently and is not shown to belong to that course before its URL is fetched.

findings.impact: An implementation conforming only to the stated FLASH relation could accept an enrolled course as an authorization decoy while reading a foreign attachment, or save caller-supplied generated content into a linked deck without proving the attachment/course relationship. This is a cross-resource authorization and outbound-fetch boundary defect.
findings.recommendation: Revise this operation row to enumerate attachmentId and courseId and require, before save, parsing, file fetch, or deck/card creation: STUDENT role; actor home institute; APPROVED enrollment in the persisted course; Attachment→SyllabusItem→Course equality with courseId; and course institute equality. Define uniform safe 404 for every foreign/mismatched child. Apply the same binding to both preview and save branches.

findings.title: Completion rewards rely on unverifiable client-asserted engagement and have no replay-bound study session

sourceEvidence.explanation: The operation accepts only deckId, cardsReviewed, and durationSeconds; no persisted study-session identifier or replay token is part of the contract.

The existing contract uses client-asserted counts and duration to trigger EXP and badge effects. It resolves the deck only by id and provides no evidence of ownership, enrollment, actual reviewed cards, elapsed server time, or one-time completion.

A persisted study-session model exists, but the assigned operation design does not identify a session input or require resolution through it. The operation matrix likewise lists only flashcardDeck and no resourceInputs.

findings.impact: A student could claim engagement repeatedly to obtain gamification effects. The revised FLASH statement that study-session IDs resolve through the owned deck is not implementable for this HTTP contract because no such identifier or replay rule is specified.
findings.recommendation: Revise the contract to require an actor-owned, institute-bound, course-authorized persisted study session (or equivalent server-issued one-time completion record), verify its deck/cards and server-observed duration, and atomically mark it completed with EXP/badge effects. Define replay/idempotency behavior. If no persisted proof is intended, remove reward-bearing effects from this endpoint.

implementationRisks.title: Course and submission routes currently retain incomplete role, institute, enrollment, and parent authorization

sourceEvidence.explanation: The baseline omits the INSTRUCTOR alias and does not enforce an instructor home-institute match.
The instructor branch reads by syllabusItemId without first binding it to route courseId or instructor assignment; the student branch lacks course enrollment and institute checks.
The baseline authenticates but does not require STUDENT role, APPROVED enrollment, or institute equality before submission upsert.
Unknown roles and SUPER_USER fall into the Admin-style all-course branch, INSTRUCTOR is omitted, and non-Admin home-institute equality is not checked.

implementationRisks.impact: Until implemented, unauthorized normal roles, unknown roles, SUPER_USER, foreign-institute actors, or unrelated instructors may read or mutate protected course data.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Implement the revised canonical actor and role resolution, fail-closed UNKNOWN/SUPER_USER handling, institute equality, persisted course relationship, enrollment/assignment, and child-parent constraints before protected reads or effects.

implementationRisks.title: Several flashcard routes currently lack the complete student, ownership, enrollment, and institute boundary

sourceEvidence.explanation: The baseline has no STUDENT check or owned-deck/institute/course-enrollment check before gamification effects.
The baseline has no explicit STUDENT role check or actor-institute equality and returns 403 rather than uniform safe 404 for a foreign linked course.
The baseline uses a different session helper, lacks explicit STUDENT denial, permits the save branch before enrollment validation, and does not bind the attachment to courseId.

implementationRisks.impact: Until remediation, non-students or students with unrelated resources may inspect files, create linked decks, fetch content, or receive gamification effects outside the FLASH capability.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Apply the revised canonical request actor and FLASH relationship checks before body-driven resource reads, parsing, external fetches, writes, EXP, or badges; return uniform safe 404 for foreign resources.

implementationRisks.title: Batch card deletion currently permits partial success for mixed owned and foreign identifiers

sourceEvidence.explanation: The baseline filters supplied ids to owned cards and deletes validIds whenever at least one matches, silently ignoring foreign or nonexistent ids.

implementationRisks.impact: A mixed batch does not fail as a complete foreign/mismatched request, creating ambiguous authorization semantics and allowing callers to probe results through deletedCount.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Require every distinct requested id to resolve through an actor-owned, same-institute deck before any delete, reject duplicates or normalize them deterministically, and return a uniform safe 404 with no deletion if the complete set cannot be authorized.

implementationRisks.title: Course-linked deck creation and reassignment currently do not verify enrollment or course institute

sourceEvidence.explanation: The baseline writes caller-supplied courseId without resolving the course, matching its institute, or proving APPROVED enrollment.
Ownership of the existing deck is checked, but a replacement courseId is accepted without validating the target course relationship.

implementationRisks.impact: Until implemented, students can create or move their decks onto foreign or unenrolled courses, violating the revised persisted relationship and institute boundary.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Resolve every non-null courseId and require same-institute APPROVED enrollment before create or reassignment; use a safe 404 for unavailable or foreign courses and perform no write on failure.

coverage.assessment: Reviewed TEACH actor selection, instructor aliases, Admin authority, course/institute assignment, submission-to-syllabus-to-course binding, grading and downstream feedback/EXP/badge/notification effects. Revised design is adequate for this operation; baseline remains unimplemented.

Reviewed COURSE_READ and STUDENT_WORK paths, syllabusItemId binding, student ownership, APPROVED enrollment, institute scope, instructor assignment, response privacy, attachment writes, and denial ordering. Revised design is adequate; baseline exposures remain implementation risks.

Reviewed relationship-constrained enumeration, supported institute selection, home-institute equality, instructor aliases, Admin scope, UNKNOWN/SUPER_USER denial, pagination inputs, and response construction. Revised design is adequate; current fallback-to-Admin behavior is an implementation risk.

Reviewed authentication, STUDENT restriction, attachment/course/enrollment binding, save and preview branches, deck/card writes, parsing, and outbound file fetch. Design fails to specify the required attachment-to-course persisted chain across both branches.

Reviewed owned-deck and institute constraints, card-to-deck resolution, progress scoping, mutation ordering, PATCH field handling, and batch deletion. Revised single-resource design is adequate; partial batch deletion remains an implementation risk requiring all-or-nothing authorization.

Reviewed STUDENT capability, owned deck, linked-course enrollment, session completion, EXP/badge effects, and replay resistance. Design lacks a verifiable persisted engagement/session contract and therefore is not ready.

Reviewed creator ownership, institute scope, optional course filtering/linking, APPROVED enrollment, create/reassignment/archive/delete effects, and denial ordering. Revised FLASH policy covers these operations; current missing linked-course checks remain implementation risks.

Reviewed STUDENT role, Attachment→SyllabusItem→Course resolution, same-institute enrollment, pre-fetch authorization, file parsing, and safe denials. Revised FLASH relationship is sufficient when implemented, though current source lacks complete enforcement.

Reviewed cardId resolution through actor-owned same-institute deck, linked-course enrollment, actor-owned progress, answer disclosure, and update/create ordering. Revised FLASH policy is adequate; baseline implementation must adopt the complete boundary.

Reviewed STUDENT restriction, owned same-institute deck, linked-course enrollment, cards and actor-specific progress resolution, serialization, and denial ordering. Revised design is adequate; baseline ownership controls are present but canonical actor and linked-course requirements remain to be implemented.

limitations: This was a document-only pre-implementation design review. No implementation, runtime, transaction, test, database, build, or formal gate evidence was claimed or evaluated.
Only the ten explicitly assigned route paths and seventeen assigned HTTP methods were reviewed. Shared policy and schema excerpts were considered only where necessary for those operations.

The packet does not supply a named list of the human twelve acceptance-criterion identifiers. affectedAC therefore uses the exact supplied policy identifiers TEACH, COURSE_READ, STUDENT_WORK, and FLASH; no unsupplied AC identities were invented.

Operational approver, manifest maintainer/release reviewer, production dataset/fingerprint attestation, expiry lifetime, and revocation runbook ownership remain required human/operator assignments. Their absence blocks production oversight disclosure but does not alter the legacy-route-specific findings above; deny-by-default remains required.
